data.narrative:
Keen Technologies is a seed-stage robotics and manufacturing company founded by John Carmack that has raised $20M to date. The comparable universe for Robotics & Manufacturing includes 1 public company (277810.KQ) and 8 private peers, including Walden Robotics, Divergent, Exotec, Locus Robotics, and Bedrock Robotics.

The stage-progression method is applicable and serves as the primary valuation anchor. Using total capital raised ($20M) as a proxy for seed-stage value and applying a typical 2.5x step-up multiplier to project the next financing round yields an implied valuation of $50M. The peer-median method could not be reliably applied due to insufficient comparable data within narrow filters—while 8 same-sector peers exist, fewer than 3 meet same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-tier criteria, making an all-sector median median unreliable.

This analysis supports a valuation range of $42M to $57M, centered at $50M. The range reflects both the stage-progression methodology and a conservative ±15% band around the point estimate. Key uncertainties include the lack of granular peer comparables at the seed stage in this sector, the reliance on a single analytical method, and the absence of current financial metrics (revenue, burn rate, unit economics) that would typically inform early-stage robotics valuations. Investors should consider Keen's competitive positioning within its peer set and financing trajectory before finalizing terms.
